articles.title: Chronic heavy metal exposure drives mitochondrial remodeling and metabolic reprogramming to enhance sperm velocity in wild tree sparrows
Compound-specific porewater-surface water relationships of taste and odor compounds under contrasting water-level conditions in a reservoir drawdown zone
Comparative assessment of the behaviour and potential ecological risks of pretilachlor and its metabolites in contrasting soil environments
Plant invasions are associated with lower community stability at multiple spatial scales
Sleep forms flexible context representations in toddlers
articles.abstract: Abstract Sleep consolidates episodic memory through a hippocampus-dependent process in adults. Whether and how sleep supports memory consolidation during early life, when hippocampal function is immature, remains unclear. Here, we examined effects of sleep on the consolidation of spatial context, a core component of episodic memory, in toddlers aged 2–3 years. Toddlers were familiarized with two spatial contexts, followed by a ~ 90-min nap or equivalent wake period. Afterwards, using a hide-and-seek game we tested their ability to relocate toys within these contexts. Only after post-familiarization sleep, toddlers showed significant context memory and formed stronger associations between toys and specific contexts compared to wakefulness. Contextual memory was positively correlated with spindle density and slow oscillation–spindle phase-amplitude coupling during non-rapid eye movement sleep. Here, we show that, despite hippocampal immaturity, memory effects in the sleeping toddler’s brain are accompanied by thalamo-cortical oscillatory dynamics that are also implicated in adult memory consolidation.

articles.title: Exocomets in a planet nursery
Targeting MDA5 induces immunogenic cell death and promotes anti-tumor immunity
Sea-level contribution from Thwaites Glacier doubles in an observation-constrained ice-sheet model
articles.abstract: Abstract Thwaites Glacier is a major contributor to Antarctic mass loss and a key source of uncertainty in future sea-level rise. Ocean-driven melting at its grounding line drives rapid retreat, yet most models treat the transition between grounded and floating ice as a sharp boundary, neglecting kilometer-scale seawater intrusions that develop as the grounding line migrates and forms a grounding zone. Here, we show that actively-melting grounding zones are required to reproduce nearly three decades of observed retreat, thinning, and acceleration of Thwaites Glacier in a calibrated ice-sheet model, with successful reconstruction occurring only when grounding zones are represented as 2-5 km wide regions. Extending this model forward, we show that grounding-zone processes govern glacier’s detachment from stabilizing seafloor ridges, enabling unpinning as early as 2038 and producing up to 30 ± 6 mm of global mean sea-level rise by 2100 - approximately double previous projections even without additional climate warming.

articles.title: Whole blood transcriptomics atlas across human diseases
articles.abstract: Abstract We present a WBT Atlas, comprising 4444 WBT samples across 98 distinct health conditions, enabling systematic exploration of disease-associated transcriptomic signatures. Health condition–specific profiles are characterized across immune, metabolic, and cell-type specific features at the gene, gene module, and pathway levels. By integrating matched plasma proteomics data from 1280 participants across 28 health conditions, we further assess blood RNA–protein relationships and demonstrate their complementary biological roles. By integrating RNA and protein signatures, we develop multi-class classification models that accurately distinguish among a wide range of health conditions, with integrated models consistently outperforming those based on single-omics data alone. The identified RNA and protein signatures are validated across ten independent WBT cohorts and the UK Biobank. Together, the WBT Atlas provides a genome-wide resource that enables translational discovery in precision medicine.

articles.title:
Perturbation of
the Reproductive Endocrine System
by Halogenated Nitrophenols via Thyroid Receptor Signaling: Implications
for Developmental, Fertility, and Intergenerational Risks in Japanese
Medaka
articles.abstract: Abstract Disinfection byproducts (DBPs) are ubiquitously formed in disinfected drinking water and wastewater effluents, with emerging aromatic DBPs constituting a large fraction and generally exhibiting higher toxicity than regulated species. However, their ecological risks remain poorly understood. Here, we focused on two typical halogenated nitrophenols, 2,6-dibromo-4-nitrophenol (2,6-DB-4-NP) and 2,6-dichloro-4-nitrophenol (2,6-DC-4-NP), and systematically evaluated their developmental and reproductive toxicity in Japanese medaka at environmentally relevant ng/L concentrations. Early-life exposure significantly delayed hatching and increased larval mortality, while a 110-day chronic exposure inhibited further gonadal development. These effects were linked to disruption of thyroid hormone homeostasis, reflected by an altered triiodothyronine/thyroxine (T3/T4) ratio and dysfunction of the hypothalamic–pituitary–thyroid (HPT) axis, which subsequently led to sex-specific dysregulation of the hypothalamic–pituitary–gonadal (HPG) axis. Males displayed elevated estrogen levels, enhanced estrogen receptor signaling, and hepatic vitellogenin synthesis, whereas females showed the opposite pattern, indicating a feminization risk and diminished estrogenic responses, respectively. Furthermore, parental exposure caused developmental impairments in the offspring, suggesting potential intergenerational toxicity. In silico docking further revealed that 14 other aromatic DBPs exhibited high-affinity binding to thyroid hormone receptors (TRα and TRβ), similar to the two halogenated nitrophenols, supporting their potential to disrupt TR-mediated signaling. Collectively, this study adds to the limited in vivo evidence of thyroid and reproductive endocrine disruption by halogenated nitrophenols under environmentally realistic conditions, underscoring their ecological significance and implicating TR signaling as a mechanistic node for future study.

articles.title:
Associations of
Early Pregnancy Contaminant Exposure
with Gestational Diabetes Mellitus and Mediation by Metabolic Pathway
Perturbations
articles.abstract: Abstract Early pregnancy exposure to environmental contaminants is a known risk factor for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), yet the metabolic pathways linking specific chemical categories to disease pathogenesis remain largely unknown. To address this gap, we conducted a meet-in-the-middle mediation analysis within a prospective birth cohort, leveraging a nested case–control study (116 GDM cases, 232 controls) with 182 contaminants across 11 chemical categories and 702 metabolites measured in early pregnancy serum samples. Seven individual contaminants showed significant associations with GDM risk, with BHT-COOH exhibiting the strongest effect (OR = 2.34, 95% CI: 1.59–3.45). Weighted quantile sum (WQS) regression indicated a positive mixture association with GDM, with Bayesian kernel machine regression (BKMR) providing a complementary assessment of mixture effects. Notably, we identified 506 exposure–metabolite pairs with significant mediation and consistent directionality, providing a comprehensive profile of candidate metabolic intermediates in the associations between contaminant exposure and GDM. Pathway-level analysis identified six candidate metabolic pathways with significant mediation effects, among which the phenylalanine, tyrosine and tryptophan biosynthesis pathway showed the largest mediation estimate, accounting for 75.5% of the DEHP/DNOP–GDM association. Similar pathway-level mediation effects were observed for both individual contaminants and the mixture exposure index. Collectively, these findings identify potential metabolic intermediates linking early pregnancy contaminant exposure to GDM and provide hypotheses for further epidemiological and experimental validation.

articles.title:
Data-Driven Accelerated
Design-Synthesis of Heterogeneous
Fenton-like Catalysts for Water Decontamination
articles.abstract: Abstract Heterogeneous Fenton-like catalysis offers an effective approach for organic pollutant removal, yet catalyst development remains largely empirical and lacks a closed-loop design-synthesis-validation framework. Here, we report a synthesis-oriented inverse-design framework for Fe-based catalysts. We first developed ML_Removal to predict pollutant removal, achieving a test-set R2 of 0.970, while SHAP analysis identified specific surface area (SSA) and Fe loading (Fe wt %) as actionable catalyst descriptors. We then built two synthesis-to-property models to predict SSA and Fe wt %, with SMOTER augmentation enhancing model performance and yielding test-set R2 of 0.782 and 0.856, respectively. Coupling these models with NSGA-II enabled the identification of candidate synthesis recipes targeting the SSA and Fe wt % windows. Two catalysts synthesized according to the NSGA-II-derived recipes exhibited measured SSA of 538.40 and 468.63 m2/g and Fe wt % of 8.19 and 7.01 wt %, aligning with the design targets. The catalysts achieved broad pollutant removal, retained activity in real waters matrices, and maintained >71% naproxen removal after five cycles. External validation of ML_Removal using the experimental data sets yielded an R2 of 0.784, demonstrating transferability to pollutants absent from the training set. Overall, this work establishes a closed-loop design–synthesis–validation framework for data-driven catalyst development and experimental realization.

articles.title:
Microbial
Degradation of Lignin Generates Iron-Binding
Organic Ligands
articles.abstract: Abstract The association of organic carbon (OC) with iron (Fe) minerals is a primary mechanism governing soil OC persistence, yet the molecular agents mediating Fe–OC binding remain poorly defined. In this study, we demonstrated that microbial degradation of lignin, one of the major contributors to soil OC, generates organic compounds with the potential to bind to Fe, with implications for mineral-associated carbon stabilization. Lignin samples were microbially degraded by Pseudomonas putida KT2440 for 30 days and subsequently reacted with FeCl3. Ultrahigh-performance liquid chromatography–high-resolution tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC–HRMS/MS)-based analysis identified 494 distinct molecular features with MS/MS data, of which 21 were identified as lignin-derived Fe-binding ligands using Fe isotopologue-enabled metabolomics. Structural annotation of 15 identified ligands further elucidated the chemical nature of the lignin-derived compounds. Systematic meta-analysis of more than 20,000 public HRMS datasets revealed that related compounds occur in soil and aquatic organic matter across diverse ecosystems, ranging from grassland to Arctic tundra. Ion identity molecular networking (IIMN) further revealed additional putative ligands and structurally related transformation products. Altogether, our findings provide a molecular framework for investigating how microbially generated Fe-binding ligands may contribute to Fe–OC interactions and potentially, soil carbon stabilization under changing climate conditions.

articles.title:
Fusion-DeepRSM
for Satellite-Derived PM2.5 Estimation and Precursor Sensitivity
Prediction
articles.abstract: Abstract Accurate estimation of fine particulate matter (PM2.5) and characterization of precursor-response relationships are crucial for human health protection and air quality management. However, current approaches remain limited by the high computational cost and uncertainties of chemical transport models (CTMs), as well as the sample imbalance and limited interpretability of observation-based machine learning methods. Here, we developed Fusion-DeepRSM, an observation-constrained extension of the Deep Learning Response Surface Model (DeepRSM) framework that integrates CTM simulations, multisource satellite observations, and ground-based measurements to derive spatially continuous PM2.5 concentrations and characterize precursor-PM2.5 response relationships. Results from ground-based observations and CTM-based testbed experiments show that Fusion-DeepRSM effectively alleviates the sample imbalance in conventional models and mitigates PM2.5 overestimation in rural regions, with an average reduction of 4.13 μg/m3 while maintaining high predictive accuracy (R2 = 0.872 and RMSE = 11.82 μg/m3). In addition, Fusion-DeepRSM successfully quantifies precursor-PM2.5 response relationships, revealing pronounced seasonal and regional heterogeneity consistent with established atmospheric chemistry understanding. With high computational efficiency, Fusion-DeepRSM further quantifies the effects of meteorological conditions and pollutant concentrations on PM2.5 variability. During the nationwide PM2.5 decline from 2020 to 2023, unfavorable meteorology partially offset pollutant-related improvements (+1.2 versus −1.8 μg/m3), while changes in precursor pollutant conditions played an important role in the February 2023 PM2.5 rebound in the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei region. These findings demonstrate the strong potential of Fusion-DeepRSM for air quality modeling and region-specific pollution mitigation.

articles.title:
Covering
and Flaring Manure Storage Units as a Methane
Mitigation Strategy for Small- to Midsize Dairy Operations in the
United States
articles.abstract: Abstract Covering manure storages and flaring the captured methane (cap-and-flare) offers a technically feasible mitigation pathway for small- and midsize dairies that has received limited attention relative to anaerobic digestion (AD). While AD systems are more economically feasible for large operations, the dairy segment with fewer than 1,000 cows still produces approximately 34% of U.S. milk and remains largely unaddressed. We estimated technical CH4 mitigation potential under full cap-and-flare adoption using the IPCC Tier 2 model for 8,675 dairy farms across 38 US states. Under 100% adoption, liquid storage CH4 mitigation potential (GWP100 = 27) ranged from 5.53 MMT CO2e yr–1 (central 90% interval: 3.70–6.63) to 10.36 (central 90% interval: 6.93–12.42) depending on the Arrhenius activation energy and reference temperature constants applied, representing 16–30% of the CO2e attributed to dairy manure CH4 in the 2022 EPA Greenhouse Gas Inventory. These values represent an upper-bound technical potential rather than a projected deployment level. Average national Levelized Costs of Mitigation (LCOM) ranged from $55 t–1 CO2e (conservative parametrization) to $29 t–1 CO2e (upper-bound parametrization), positioning cap-and-flare as a cost-efficient CH4 mitigation option. Existing USDA-NRCS Conservation Practice Standard 367 provides an available incentive mechanism, although meaningful scale-up will likely require dedicated funding for infrastructure and technical assistance. These results suggest that cap-and-flare could complement AD as a mitigation pathway for U.S. dairy operations where AD is not economically viable.

articles.title:
Greenhouse Gas and
Ammonia Emission Factors from Raw
and Digested Cattle Slurry: A Field-Based Synthesis for Cattle Systems
articles.abstract: Abstract Anaerobic digestion (AD) of cattle slurry is widely promoted as a manure-management strategy, yet its effects on greenhouse gas (GHG) and ammonia (NH3) emissions remain uncertain. This review provides the first field-based synthesis of paired methane (CH4), nitrous oxide (N2O), and NH3 emission factors (EFs) from raw and digested cattle slurry during storage and land application. A total of 98 paired observations from 16 studies were analyzed using paired bootstrap geometric mean ratios. AD reduced dry matter, volatile solids, and carbon content while increasing total ammoniacal nitrogen (TAN) and pH. Consequently, digestate CH4 EFs during storage were 51% lower than those of raw slurry (p = 0.001). In contrast, NH3–N EFs increased by 63% during storage (p = 0.071) and by 40% following land application (p = 0.003). However, TAN-normalized NH3 EFs did not differ between manure types, suggesting similar volatilization potential. AD had no significant effect on N2O EFs. A system-level analysis showed that AD reduced total GHG emissions across the storage-to-land-application continuum by 49%, although this benefit was partially offset by increased NH3 losses. These findings identify AD as an effective CH4 mitigation strategy for cattle slurry when combined with targeted NH3 abatement measures to maximize environmental benefits.

articles.title: A method quantifying soil melanin to understand fungal impacts on soil carbon stability
articles.abstract: Abstract Fungal necromass, particularly dead microbial cells rich in melanin, is an important contributor to long-term soil carbon stabilization. Progress in understanding the role of soil melanin is limited by the lack of validated analytical methods. DNA-based approaches estimate only the genetic potential for melanin production and therefore provide indirect evidence of melanin occurrence. To directly assess soil melanin, we evaluated spectroscopic and spectrophotometric assays; however, both approaches proved insufficiently specific due to interference from chemically related compounds. Here, we introduce a liquid chromatography method that enables quantification of major fungal melanin types in soils. By enabling direct quantification of fungal melanin in soil, this framework allows longstanding hypotheses regarding melanized fungal necromass and soil carbon stabilization to be tested mechanistically. Here, we show with the proposed method that soil melanin concentrations are strongly correlated with total soil carbon, supporting a central role for fungal melanin in long-term soil carbon stabilization.

articles.title: GlycoStamp-seq: Single-cell nascent sialoglycometabolomics captures sialylation dynamics in immune cells of an oxaliplatin-treated bladder cancer mouse model
Time-lapse RESOLFT nanoscopy empowered by deep learning
articles.abstract: Abstract Capturing the dynamic interplay of proteins and organelles within cells requires microscopy methods with high spatial and temporal resolution. Reversible Saturable OpticaL Fluorescent Transition (RESOLFT) demonstrated great potential for live cell nanoscopy by using patterned light and reversibly switching fluorescent probes. Despite the latest improvement in both switching probes and optical schemes, the duration and frame rate of the time-lapse are still limited by photobleaching and spatial sampling steps. Here, we present two distinct strategies based on deep learning to restore low signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) or under-sampled images pushing the experimental boundaries of RESOLFT. We demonstrate the capability of Hierarchical DivNoising (HDN) to restore low-SNR RESOLFT data while maintaining full spatial resolution, both in supervised and unsupervised settings. This allows a 10-fold reduction of light dose per frame, and up to 5 times longer imaging. Then, we present Fast-MoNaLISA, a method that reduces the acquisition time of any point-scanning systems. This allows a 4-fold increase in frame rate, and a reduction of scanning artefacts. Overall, our methods open up possibilities for dynamic data acquisition at the sub-organelle level, such as vesicles budding in and out from intact mitochondria, or the actin meshwork formation and dissociation.

articles.title: Asymmetric bloom lengthening drives high-latitude ocean chlorophyll accumulation imbalance
In situ reduction-driven formation of sub-nanometer alternating heterostructures
ETSAM: effectively segmenting cell membranes in cryo-electron tomograms
Inhomogeneity of negative enthalpy enables excellent mechanical properties in nanosized single crystals of multi-principal element alloys
articles.abstract: Abstract Many nanosized metals with limited dislocation nucleation and multiplication usually exhibit poor plasticity. Previous studies have demonstrated that multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) can achieve a combination of strength and plasticity. However, whether these mechanical properties extend to their nanosized counterparts and how nanosized MPEAs accommodate plastic deformation remains unknown. Using a homemade in-situ device, we captured the atomic-scale tensile process and measured the stress-strain curve of Fe 48 Mn 32 Co 10 Cr 10 nanosized single crystals (NSCs). We find that NSCs achieve a strength of ~3 GPa and a uniform elongation of ~20%. We show that this combination arises from the inhomogeneous distribution of enthalpy, which produces a broad spectrum of energy barriers for the nucleation of full dislocations, partial dislocations, and nanotwins. Consequently, dislocations and nanotwins are randomly generated throughout MPEA NSCs, effectively suppressing local stress concentration and leading to both high strength and large uniform elongation.

articles.title: Intensification of near-inertial currents in the Atlantic Ocean over the past two decades
HCV incidence and prevalence trends among people who use drugs in France 2004 to 2023
articles.abstract: Abstract Hepatitis C virus (HCV) remains a key public health challenge, particularly among people who use and inject drugs (PWUD, PWID). While direct-acting antivirals (DAA) have revolutionized HCV treatment, meeting the WHO’s 2030 elimination target requires accurate estimation of incidence and prevalence to guide prevention and care. We analyze cross-sectional surveys conducted in France in 2004, 2013, and 2023, recruiting PWUD at harm reduction services and collecting behavioral and biological data. We estimate age-and time-dependent prevalence of HCV antibodies and HCV RNA using multivariate regression models while incidence was estimated from two-state transmission models. The demographic profile of PWUD has aged over time (mean age 35 years in 2004 vs. 44 in 2023) while injection prevalence remained stable (61.7% in 2023). Between 2013 and 2023, HCV burden declined substantially: HCV RNA prevalence fell from 19.4% (95% CI 16.3–23.0) to 9.5% (7.2–12.3) among all PWUD, and from 29.6% to 14.5% among PWID. Incidence among PWID decreased from 6.5 (4.1–8.0) to 2.4 (1.4–4.2) per 100 person-years. These reductions likely reflect the combined impact of DAA scale-up and harm reduction policies, marking substantial progress toward elimination targets. However, ongoing transmission highlights persistent barriers requiring targeted public health actions.

articles.title: An automated operon refactoring workflow for heterologous expression of non-ribosomal peptide biosynthetic gene clusters
A supergene and genomic mosaicism are associated with phenotypic evolution in Galápagos tree finches
articles.abstract: Abstract Adaptive radiations provide powerful models to study the origins of phenotypic novelty and species diversity. Darwin’s finches constitute a classic example of adaptive radiation, in which beak morphology is a key trait related to fitness. Here, we focus on Camarhynchus tree finches by analyzing whole genomes in combination with morphological data to revisit long-standing questions regarding their origins raised before genetic evidence became available. Camarhynchus diversified over the last 100,000 years, yielding some striking morphological differences despite shallow genetic divergence. We identify several highly differentiated loci, including G03 , a supergene affecting beak and body size. We reveal a striking example of genomic mosaicism, in which autosomal differentiation between two sympatric species is restricted primarily to a single locus -( G03 )- that approaches fixation, shifting them from one phenotypic optimum to another. Contextualized in a broader phylogenetic framework, we also reveal an unexpected diversity of G03 haplotypes and show that the small and large G03 alleles diverged early in the radiation, suggesting a key genetic innovation enabling ecological expansion among species of Darwin’s finches. Our results further establish Camarhynchus as a model example of speciation with gene flow, underscoring the broader role of hybridization in generating biodiversity.

articles.title: Long-term nitrous acid evolution modulates ozone and secondary aerosol variations in global megacities
Preserved higher-order mentalising during strategic interactions after medial prefrontal cortex damage
articles.abstract: Abstract Mentalising, the ability to infer the beliefs and intentions of others, is essential for successful social interaction. Previous studies have implicated the medial prefrontal cortex in mentalising, but whether this region is necessary for higher-order mentalising remains unclear. Here we show that people with focal damage to the medial prefrontal cortex retain the ability to engage in higher-order mentalising during a strategic social game. We compare their performance with patients with brain damage in other regions and lesion-free participants. Individuals with medial prefrontal cortex damage achieve similar rewards and use comparable mentalising strategies, but they are slower when making strategic decisions. Computational modelling indicates that this slowing reflects a greater tendency to require evidence before committing to a choice. Voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping identifies medial prefrontal regions linked to altered decision processes rather than mentalising. These findings suggest that the medial prefrontal cortex supports strategic decisions while higher-order mentalising remains intact.

articles.title: Fruit-eating adaptations in a Late Cretaceous oviraptorosaur (Theropoda)
articles.abstract: Abstract The diversification of herbivorous dinosaurs and the rise of angiosperms in the Late Cretaceous are each well established, but the link between them is debated. Broad-scale diversity patterns in the two groups appear not to closely align, and there is no direct evidence of dinosaur adaptation to angiosperm-based diets. Here we describe Infernogallus jamesi gen. et. sp. nov., a diminutive caenagnathid oviraptorosaur, and show that these theropods were specialised herbivores that originated alongside the rise of fleshy angiosperm fruits. The nearly complete, articulated skull of Infernogallus jamesi —the first for the clade—reveals drastic changes to the adductor musculature organisation, unique in non-avian theropods but converged upon by extant frugivorous parrots. These modifications enabled extensive oral processing of soft food using anteroposterior movement of the mandible and occlusion of ridges and grooves on opposed elements. Altogether, this attests to a highly specialised herbivorous diet in caenagnathids, which likely consisted in large part of fleshy angiosperm fruits, which increased in size and diversity in concert with the radiation of oviraptorosaurs. Caenagnathids thus provide one of the strongest candidates for angiosperm-based diet adaptations in dinosaurs, but their role in the Late Cretaceous proliferation of fruit—which shaped early Cenozoic flora—remains unclear.

articles.title:
Correction
to “Nonlinear
Responses of Anaerobic
Methane Oxidation to Water Table Drawdown in Peatlands”

Repositioning Wastewater
Sludge in the Urban Carbon
Cycle: A Conceptual Pathway to Sustainable Aviation Fuels

Strengthening
Care
for Twin Pregnancies in the Context
of Assisted Reproduction: Emphasizing the Effects of Environmental
Exposures on Birth Outcomes

Combined Residues
of Frequently Detected Herbicides
are Stronger Predictors of Soil Resistome and Virulence Potential
than Single Residues
articles.abstract: Abstract Overuse of herbicides has resulted in a global epidemic of evolved resistance in soil ecosystems. While single herbicide risk has been documented, the impact of multiple herbicide residues on the soil resistomes remains poorly understood. Our study quantified the residues of 24 herbicides, profiled antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and virulence factor genes (VFGs), and reconstructed 1086 metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) from 93 agricultural soils across China. The analytical results demonstrate that the frequently detected herbicide residues (e.g., 60–90% detection frequency) are stronger predictors of soil antibiotic resistomes than total herbicide load, unsupervised mixture based on principal component analysis (PCA), or single-herbicide models. For VFG abundance, the same mixture outperformed the best single herbicide and total herbicide concentration, although PCA–PC1 showed a moderately stronger correlation. Specifically, these commonly detected herbicides showed positive associations with ARG abundance through both direct linkages and bacterial community-dependent indirect pathways. Similar patterns were observed for virulence potential, where frequently detected residues maintained strong predictive performance and were predominantly associated with indirect pathways. Functional annotation patterns further suggest a concurrent enrichment of traits related to antioxidant defense, mobility, adherence, and immune modulation under elevated herbicide exposure. Notably, multiple herbicide residues were linked to the abundance of a Trinickia taxon, which was identified as a candidate ARG-VFG co-occurrence MAG carrying a high ARG load. Our findings highlight the need to integrate compound exposure of frequently detected herbicides into future risk assessment methodology for preventing the dissemination of ARGs in agricultural soils.

articles.title:
Soil
Protists Consume Viruses to Drive Microbial Nutrient
Cycling: Overlooked Trophic Pathways in Soil Food Web
articles.abstract: Abstract Soil viruses are traditional top-down regulators that redistribute organic matter through host lysis and the viral shunt, implicitly positioning them as terminal sinks rather than active trophic components. Here, we show, for the first time, that soil viruses can also be direct prey for protists, establishing an overlooked pathway for the transfer of viral-derived nutrients and energy within soil food webs. In controlled cocultures, the ciliate Tetrahymena pyriformis actively ingested the soil bacteriophage HRZ04p, with viral abundance declining by 0.66-log within 24 h at a virus-to-protist ratio of 5:1. Under high viral availability (104:1), viral consumption enhanced protist population growth by 2.24-fold relative to virus-free controls. Viral grazing altered nutrient dynamics, characterized by ammonium peaking at 1,206 μg L–1 (a 92% increase compared with protists alone) and coordinated shifts in nitrogen-metabolizing enzymes. Untargeted metabolomics revealed extensive metabolic reprogramming, with amino acid catabolic pathways upregulated. In contrast, amino acid biosynthesis and aminoacyl-tRNA biosynthesis were simultaneously activated, reflecting recycling of viral-derived substrates into new protein synthesis. These findings confirm the existence of a soil “viral consumption” pathway, reposition viruses as active nodes within microbial food webs, and provide a mechanistic and conceptual foundation for incorporating virus-mediated nutrient fluxes into soil biogeochemical models.

articles.title:
Lattice-Oxygen-Mediated
Electronic Reconstruction
of High-Entropy Oxides for Durable Fenton-like Water Treatment
articles.abstract: Abstract High-entropy catalysts offer broad compositional tunability for peroxymonosulfate (PMS)-based water treatment, yet achieving rapid, selective, and durable oxidation remains challenging because metallic bonding in high-entropy alloys (HEAs) limits electronic communication among metal sites. Here, we construct a quinary high-entropy oxide (HEO, (FeCoNiMnCu)3O4) featuring an oxygen-bridged M-O-M framework that enables local electronic coupling among neighboring metal centers. X-ray absorption spectroscopy and theoretical calculations support oxygen-mediated charge redistribution, with Hirshfeld analysis indicating 0.46e of charge transfer toward adsorbed PMS. Temperature-dependent electrochemical impedance spectroscopy reveals a substantially lower apparent activation energy for interfacial charge transfer in the HEO (0.43 eV) than in the HEA (1.15 eV). Mechanistic experiments support a predominantly nonradical PMS activation pathway involving high-valent cobalt-oxo species and singlet oxygen. The HEO achieved near-complete phenol degradation and 87.9% total organic carbon removal within 10 min, with an apparent rate constant of 0.359 min–1 versus 0.113 min–1 for the HEA. The system maintained >90% phenol removal across pH 3–11, sustained activity over 30 reuse cycles, and retained effective contaminant removal during continuous-flow operation and 50 L bench-scale treatment. These results support lattice-oxygen-mediated electronic reconstruction as a strategy for coupling efficient PMS activation with structural durability in high-entropy oxide catalysts.

articles.title:
Phage Lysis Associated
with Biodegradable Microplastics
Mediates Microbial Physiological Adaptation to Transform Organic Matter
in Soil
articles.abstract: Abstract Biodegradable microplastics (MPs) profoundly impact the storage and stability of soil organic matter (SOM), yet the mechanisms by which phages mediate the transformation of plant- and microbially derived SOM under biodegradable MP perturbation remain poorly understood. This study integrated multiomics, stable isotope techniques, and phage inoculation experiments to investigate how phages mediate SOM transformation following biodegradable MP addition in agricultural soil. The results revealed that lytic phage-bacteria interactions were central to MP-dependent SOM transformation. Polylactic acid (PLA) reduced plant-derived organic molecules by 15% without affecting microbially derived carbon. PLA increased phage lysis and enriched auxiliary metabolic genes (AMGs) such as queC (2.2-fold increase), which supports phage replication and reduces microbial biomass. Pure culture experiments supported that PLA increased phage lytic infectivity. Phage inoculation further revealed that lytic phages accelerated bacteria to shift toward catabolism (e.g., lignocellulose degradation, citrate cycle) in PLA-amended soil, reducing carbon use efficiency (CUE) and accelerating decomposition of plant- and microbially derived carbon through viral shunt. In comparison, polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA) increased microbially derived molecules by 37%, particularly amino nitrogen compounds. The higher degradability of PHA stimulated lytic phage bloom with their hosts and enriched biosynthesis-related AMGs (e.g., cysH, glmS). Phage inoculation experiments showed that surviving bacteria assimilated phage lysate products into anabolism (e.g., amino acid and amino sugar biosynthesis), enriching metabolites such as l-isoleucine and MurNAc after PHA addition. This increased CUE and accumulation of microbial organics through viral shuttle. These findings uncover phage-mediated mechanisms linking microplastic perturbation to soil carbon cycling.

articles.title:
Unveiling
the Role of the Soil Matrix in Trichloroethylene
Degradation by Ball-Milled Sulfidated Microscale Zero-Valent Iron
articles.abstract: Abstract Ball-milled sulfidated microscale zerovalent iron (S-mZVIbm) is highly effective in degrading trichloroethylene (TCE) in anoxic water. This study investigated its performance and soil-mediated regulation in a soil-water mixed system (SWMS) using two natural soils. The results show that soil addition markedly enhanced the reactivity of S-mZVIbm. Compared with the aqueous system, the degradation rate constant of TCE (kTCE) exhibited a 6.0–8.4-fold increase at a soil-to-water ratio (S/W) of 0.5 to 2.0, while H2 production concurrently increased 210%–450%. This activation was accompanied by a decrease in apparent electron efficiency from 74.3% in water to 15.9%–27.6% in SWMS. S-mZVIbm retained higher reactivity in SWMS than in water across pH 6–10, with a maximum kTCE of 0.26 h–1 at pH 8.0. SEM, XPS, and component-specific experiments indicated that soil-mediated surface restructuring and Fe(II) redistribution-induced depassivation increased the accessibility of Fe0-rich domains, whereas organic matter and Ca/Mg-bearing phases imposed inhibitory effects. Sulfidation suppressed H2 evolution and reduced soil-specific variability under multicontaminant conditions involving TCE, carbon tetrachloride, nitrobenzene, and perchloroethylene. These results identify soil as an active regulator of Fe0 accessibility and electron allocation rather than a passive reaction medium, providing a mechanistic basis for site-specific S-mZVIbm remediation.

articles.title:
Aerosol Deposition
in the Human Respiratory System
from Distinct Urban Sources Using Multiple Exposure Metrics
articles.abstract: Abstract Targeting specific aerosol sources offers more effective air-quality control than focusing solely on ambient concentrations. Using source apportionment, major contributors to particle number concentrations in the diameter range of 6–1000 nm in urban background of Budapest, Hungary were identified, and their size distributions applied in lung deposition modelling under reference breathing conditions. In this study, we find that most particles penetrate to the deep lung with a maximum deposition at airway generations 17 to 21 depending on physical activity. Deposition fractions vary substantially by source, ranging from 76% (new particle formation) to 27% (solid fuel combustion). Exercise enhances overall deposition, and redistributes the deposited particles within the respiratory tract by decreasing extra-thoracic deposition and increasing the alveolar fraction. Our results also show that deposition rates are more sensitive to physical activity than deposition fractions. These deposition curves exhibit a levelling-off tendency in the extra-thoracic region, while continuing to increase in the lung. Particle number and particle surface area deposition curves are similar in shape, although the relative importance of aerosol sources and the most affected respiratory regions differ. We point that surface-density deposition rates are three orders of magnitude higher in the nose and mouth than in the lung.

articles.title:
Expansion of Freshwater
Harmful Cyanobacteria in Brackish
Waters: Salt Stress Responses, Toxigenic Dynamics, and Ecological
Risks along the Freshwater-to-Marine Continuum
articles.abstract: Abstract In recent years, freshwater harmful cyanobacterial blooms (CyanoHABs) and their associated cyanotoxins have been increasingly detected in estuaries and coastal lagoons, indicating that some freshwater taxa can survive in low-to-moderate salinity and may maintain their toxigenic potential in brackish environments. These observations highlight the need to understand the distribution, persistence, and ecological risks of freshwater harmful cyanobacteria across connected aquatic systems. This review synthesizes global field and mechanistic evidence on the expansion of freshwater harmful cyanobacteria along the freshwater–to–marine continuum. Hydrodynamic processes facilitate downstream transport, while salinity gradients regulate cyanobacterial survival and physiological responses. Salt stress induces cellular damage but also triggers adaptive physiological responses supporting survival. The persistence of freshwater harmful cyanobacteria in these systems is shaped by both species- and strain-level differences in salt tolerance, as well as physiological conditioning and environmental conditions experienced during transport. In addition, salinity influences cyanotoxin production, release, partitioning between particulate and dissolved fractions, and environmental persistence, thereby influencing ecological risks in brackish waters. Overall, this review synthesizes cyanobacterial adaptation and cyanotoxin dynamics along the freshwater–to–marine continuum and emphasizes integrated monitoring and modeling to support risk assessment and management of CyanoHABs.

articles.title:
Neglecting Changes
in Salinity and Tidal Range Overstates
Projected Increases in Greenhouse Gas Emissions from Mangrove Sediments
articles.abstract: Abstract Mangroves are important coastal blue carbon ecosystems, but future sediment GHG emissions remain uncertain because global projections have largely emphasized atmospheric climate drivers, with less attention to coastal hydrology, particularly sea-surface salinity and tidal range. Here, we compiled 810 sediment GHG flux measurements from 294 mangrove sites worldwide and used machine learning to project emissions to 2050, distinguishing climate-driven changes from the additional effects of projected shifts in sea-surface salinity and tidal range. We estimate a mangrove sediment GHG budget of ∼194 Tg CO2e yr–1 across reliably predicted mangrove areas worldwide around 2020. By 2050 under SSP5–8.5, projected changes in salinity and tidal range counteracted 41% of the climate-driven increase in emissions globally, with comparable offset effects among CO2, CH4, and N2O. Hydrological offset effects were strongest at 10–20° latitude in both hemispheres and weakened toward the equator and higher latitudes. Regionally, hydrological offset effects were greatest in East Africa, whereas the Indo-Pacific showed the largest absolute hydrology-driven reductions in emission budgets, largely owing to its extensive mangrove area. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating sea-surface salinity and tidal range into future projections of mangrove sediment GHG emissions under global change.

articles.title:
Aging of Urban Traffic
Fine Particles Modulates Toxicity
Mechanisms and Oxidative Stress Responses
articles.abstract: Abstract Vehicular emissions are an important source of urban air pollution that can age through atmospheric processes, but how their health effects change during atmospheric aging remains poorly understood. To simulate realistic urban emissions, we sampled air in a parking garage where cold-start and urban emissions coexist. Following aging in an oxidation flow reactor (OFR), we studied the cellular and acellular effects of the fresh and aged aerosols. Photochemical aging in the OFR increased secondary organic aerosol (SOA) mass by up to 6.9-fold, the oxygen-to-carbon (O:C) ratio from 0.26 to 0.79, and both the intrinsic oxidative potential (OPm) and the volume-normalized oxidative potential (OPv). In contrast, the peroxide-sensitive DCF activity decreased following aging. Cellular exposure to aged aerosol extracts increased cellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) formation in lung (A549) and liver (HepG2) cells, whereas fresh extracts strongly reduced cellular respiration, particularly in HepG2 cells. Cell painting analysis showed distinct morphological profiles. Exposure to aged extracts showed greater oxidative stress and DNA damage responses than those of exposure to fresh extracts. These findings suggest that atmospheric aging shifts the toxicity of fresh emissions from suppression of mitochondrial respiration toward oxygenated organics that can drive intracellular oxidative stress and DNA damage phenotypes. In conclusion, atmospheric aging of cold-start and urban vehicular emissions contributes to enhanced SOA formation and leads to distinct biological outcomes that depend on the degree of oxidative aging.

articles.title:
Synthetic DNA Tracers
Enable Ultra-High-Reproducibility
Characterization of Aquifer Hydraulic Conductivity and Contaminant
Transport
articles.abstract: Abstract Reliable characterization of aquifer hydraulic conductivity (K) via tracer-based methods remains a major challenge due to environmental background noise. We report that synthetic DNA tracers, free of background-noise interference, enable highly reproducible tomographic inversion of K fields across six replicate experiments conducted in a heterogeneous laboratory sandbox measuring 180 cm (length) × 10 cm (width) × 90 cm (height) at a steady flow rate of approximately 177.4 cm3 min–1. The results demonstrate superior reproducibility of the DNA tracers relative to dye tracers across three evaluation levels: travel-time consistency, where the contrast is most pronounced (mean R2 = 0.84 for DNA tracers versus R2 = 0.10 for dye tracers), inverted lnK field coherence, and prediction-level robustness. Contaminant-transport forecasts under four scenarios, spanning pulse versus continuous releases and conservative versus decaying solutes, further indicate that DNA-derived K fields yield substantially more stable predictions than dye-derived K fields in nearly all cases. These advantages arise from the standardized molecular design of oligonucleotides and their sequence-specific quantitation via qPCR, which collectively mitigate background interference and tracer-specific transport artifacts. These findings show that synthetic DNA tracers constitute a promising tool for aquifer characterization, addressing a critical gap in tracer-based tomography for groundwater investigations.
